issues.evidence: manual: add a; fail a; add b --depends-on a -> 'added b (pending)', stays pending forever
issues.summary: A job added after its dependency failed is left pending instead of cancelled, so it can never run.
The fixed temp-file name and lack of locking let concurrent invocations clobber each other.

issues.evidence: static/A-ruff.txt: 20 findings (UP031 percent-format, B904, C901 main)
issues.summary: Minor lint findings: percent formatting, a missing exception chain, and a complex main.
Minor lint findings: complex functions, missing exception chains, and long lines.

blinding_guess.why: The two are structurally near-identical; A ships a test suite, which weakly hints at a more process-driven build, but nothing is conclusive.

notes: Both implementations pass all 21 black-box probes; probes adapt only the --depends-on syntax (A: space-separated, B: comma-separated). Neither side has security findings beyond bandit lows in A's test subprocess use. A cycle cannot be formed through add alone because unknown dependencies are rejected, so P08 tests cycle detection on a hand-edited state file. The main differentiator is A's 15 passing tests versus B having none, against B's handling of jobs added under an already-failed dependency. Probes were run with python3.11 because the system python3.9 lacks sys.stdlib_module_names.
